newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to review 1997/98 farm price budget data.
newsitem.headline: Commission to review 1997/98 farm price budget data.

text.p: The European Commission is reviewing budget data with the aim of presenting a proposal for the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package next week, chief Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said on Wednesday.
"There are elements which one needs to look at more carefully," Van der Pas told a news briefing after the EU's 20 commissioners had discussed funding options at a weekly meeting.
Van der Pas noted that one element was the great fluctuation of the dollar rate and its consequences for market prices and the agricultural budget.
Commission sources estimated that the recent strengthening of the dollar had resulted in a 200-million-Ecu saving in EU farm export subsidies and other payments.
According to the latest estimates, savings of only 500 million Ecus were needed, compared with 1.1 billion Ecus a week ago, they said.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is seeking to persuade his colleagues that no cuts are needed in farm prices in order to keep within the 1998 budget, an aide said.
Fischler argues that the 500 million Ecus could be saved if the dollar's strength is maintained and by other factors such as a downwards revision in estimated arable aid payments.

But he is insisting on the need for 1.4 billion Ecus of cuts in farmers' compensatory payments, consisting of seven percent for cereals and four percent for oilseeds as well as a 27 percent cut in set-aside aid.
EU aid payments to cereals and oilseed farmers total 16 to 17 billion Ecus annually, representing 40 percent of the farm budget and 20 percent of total EU expenditure.
But Van der Pas said the EU commissioners had little scope to adjust the figures.
"The margin for manoeuvre is extremely tight if we want to respect a budgetary discipline as strict as that of member states," he stressed.

Although three percent growth was envisaged in the EU budget in 1998, it is practically all earmarked for regional development and other structural spending. It would allow only a 0.5 percent rise in the 1998 farm budget to 41 billion Ecus.
